wolfbook.systemKernel.markdownDescription: Path to the Wolfram kernel executable, or `Automatic` to use the first detected installation. Run the **Wolfbook: Select Kernel** command (`wolfbook.selectKernel`) to pick from all detected kernels.

wolfbook.activeSystemPrompt.markdownDescription: Name of the active @wolfbook system prompt preset (matches a file in `~/.wolfbook/prompts/<name>.md`). Set per-workspace so different projects can use different prompt styles. Change via **Wolfbook: Notebook Settings** → Copilot Instructions.

wolfbook.mcpEnabled.markdownDescription: Enable the MCP (Model Context Protocol) server so Claude and other MCP agents can connect to this window's Wolfbook tools. Disable to prevent external agent connections. Requires window reload to take effect.

wolfbook.remote.allowHostExtension.markdownDescription: Allow the **Wolfbook Remote Host** companion extension (`wolfbook.wolfbook-remote-host`) to drive this window via the `wolfbook.remote.*` command surface. Each workspace also requires a one-time consent prompt the first time the host extension connects. Set to `false` to disable the remote bridge entirely.

wolfbook.remote.checkpointDirectoryName.markdownDescription: Subpath inside the notebook's `.img/` sidecar directory where `wolfbook_remote_checkpoint` files are written. Each notebook gets its own checkpoint history; the agent reads back prior checkpoints via standard file tools.

wolfbook.remote.mirrorWolfbookToolUsage.markdownDescription: Forward Wolfbook MCP tool invocations (run cell, edit cell, etc.) to paired iOS devices via the Wolfbook Remote Host as a live activity timeline. Disable to keep tool usage local.

wolfbook.collabMode.markdownDescription: Enable Collab mode: the AI agent works in a right-column split editor while the user keeps focus in the left editor. Agent cell reveals and highlights appear in the right pane without disturbing the user's cursor or scroll position.

wolfbook.copilotPrePromptPresets.markdownDescription: Named pre-prompt presets for the @wolfbook chat participant. Each key is a preset name, value is the pre-prompt text.

wolfbook.advanced.lsp.ServerLogDirectory.description: Directory for the Wolfram LSP server log

wolfbook.lsp.ignoreUnicodeCharacters.description: Ignore Unicode characters in LSP diagnostics (e.g., Greek letters like α, β, γ)

wolfbook.editor.globalSymbolColor.description: Color applied to Global` context symbols (user-defined variables). Leave empty or set to 'auto' for automatic theme-aware color (#7eb3d4 on dark themes, #333333 on light). Set to 'off' or 'none' to disable. Accepts any CSS color string.

wolfbook.notebook.rendering.invertBright.description: When an expression is evaluated, this option specifies whether the brightness of the images in the output should be inverted in dark and high contrast themes.

Genuine HTML export like Wolfram Cloud

wolfbook.notebook.rendering.lineBreaking.description: Automatically wrap long mathematical expressions (WLLatex mode) across multiple lines based on the notebook container width.

Indentation step (in spaces) used after line breaks.
Maximum recursion depth for delimiter-internal line breaking.
Maximum refinement iterations when pixel-width line breaking is enabled.
Use compact multiline layout in line-broken output.

wolfbook.notebook.rendering.trigOmitPare.description: Omit parentheses around a single-symbol trig argument: \sin(\phi) → \sin\phi.

wolfbook.notebook.rendering.trigPowerFor.description: Move the exponent onto the trig command when the base is a parenthesised trig expression: (\sin\phi)² → \sin²\phi.

wolfbook.formatter.pageLength.description: Target line width for the Wolfbook WL code formatter. Default: 150.

wolfbook.formatter.replaceNamedChars.description: When formatting, replace \[Name] escape sequences with their UTF-8 Unicode characters (e.g. \[Alpha] → α).

wolfbook.formatter.replaceMultiply.description: When formatting with Option+Shift+F (UTF mode), replace explicit * multiplication operators with implicit multiplication (a space), e.g. a*b → a b. Preserves *= (TimesBy). Off by default; always enabled in UTF format mode.

wolfbook.formatter.autoFormat.description: Automatically format the current cell when Enter is pressed (new line). Disabled by default.

wolfbook.notebook.textOutput.pageWidth.description: Maximum line width when exporting notebook output to a text (.wls) file via 'Open as text'

wolfbook.notebook.print.pageWidth.description: Kernel $PageWidth for Print[] output (characters per line). Default 156 = 2× the Mathematica default of 78.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_remote_checkpoint
languageModelTools.modelDescription: REQUIRED USAGE — agent working memory. Persist a structured checkpoint (plan, decision, finding, summary, or blocker) for the active Wolfbook notebook. The checkpoint is saved to disk under the notebook's .img/ sidecar directory AND mirrored to any paired iOS device watching the workspace. The tool's reply lists prior checkpoints for the same notebook, so the agent should call this tool at session start (with kind='summary' to read prior context) and after every meaningful step (decisions, findings, plan updates, blockers). Treat the checkpoint history as your durable working memory across sessions.

kind.description: Checkpoint category. 'plan' = next steps; 'decision' = chosen approach with rationale; 'finding' = empirical result or insight; 'summary' = recap of session/sub-task; 'blocker' = unresolved problem requiring user input.

summary.description: One-line headline (≤ 120 chars). Shown on the iOS timeline as the primary text.

detail.description: Multi-paragraph markdown body. Include rationale, code snippets, links to cells, etc. Becomes the file body.

relatedCells.description: Optional list of CellIds this checkpoint references.

relatedFiles.description: Optional list of workspace-relative file paths this checkpoint references.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_getNotebookContext
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Multi-purpose notebook tool. action="read" (default): returns structured text of all cells (sources, section headings, and outputs as readable text — InputForm for expressions, LaTeX preview for math, plain text for Print output) for the active or named notebook. Each cell includes a stable CellId — use it for edits/moves/deletes since cell numbers shift after structural changes. Pass startCell/endCell to read only a range (useful for large notebooks). action="list": lists all currently open notebooks by filename. action="switch": switch the active editor to the notebook given by the 'notebook' filename. action="save": save the active (or named) notebook to disk. Call this FIRST to understand notebook state before making edits.

action.description: Operation to perform: 'read' (default) returns full notebook contents, 'list' lists open notebooks, 'switch' activates a notebook, 'save' saves to disk, 'summary'/'brief' (aliases) return a compact one-line-per-cell overview.

notebook.description: Optional filename of a specific open notebook (e.g. 'prototype.wb'). Required for action='switch'. If omitted for 'read'/'save', uses the active notebook.

startCell.description: Optional: 1-based cell number to start reading from. Defaults to 1. Use with endCell to read a specific range.

endCell.description: Optional: 1-based cell number to end at (inclusive). Defaults to the last cell. Use with startCell to read a specific range.

brief.description: If true, return a compact one-line-per-cell summary (number, kind, first line, output preview) instead of full source and outputs. Faster for large notebooks when you only need to locate a cell.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_evaluateExpression
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Evaluates a Wolfram Language expression in the active notebook's live kernel and returns the result as InputForm text. CRITICAL — multi-expression pitfall: passing multiple lines WITHOUT semicolons in single-expression mode (multiLine:false) causes the kernel to interpret newline-separated subexpressions as Times[...] multiplication, NOT as sequential statements — always use explicit semicolons (;) between statements, or set multiLine:true. Set multiLine:true to evaluate each non-empty line as a separate, independent expression — results are labeled Out[1]=, Out[2]=, etc.; lines ending with ; are evaluated silently. State accumulates across lines. Use outputForm to control the result format: 'Short' for truncated previews of large expressions, 'TeXForm' for LaTeX, 'MatrixForm'/'TableForm' for structured display. Default timeout is 30 s. Do not use for long-running computations.

expression.description: A valid Wolfram Language expression to evaluate.

timeoutSeconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for result (default: 30).

outputForm.description: Wrap the result in the chosen form before returning. 'Short' truncates large expressions (useful for previewing), 'TeXForm' returns LaTeX, 'MatrixForm'/'TableForm' for matrices/tables. Default: InputForm.

multiLine.description: If true, the expression is split on newlines (\n) and each non-empty line is evaluated as a SEPARATE, COMPLETE Wolfram Language expression — exactly like pressing Shift+Enter on each line one by one. Results are returned labeled Out[1]=, Out[2]=, etc. Lines ending with ; are evaluated silently (output suppressed). State accumulates across lines. IMPORTANT: each line must be a syntactically complete WL expression on its own (e.g. "f[x_] := x^2" on one line). Multi-line WL constructs must be collapsed to a single line before passing. The separator is always \n (newline character); do NOT use semicolons as the line separator — use ; only to suppress output within a single expression.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_lookupSymbol
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Look up a Wolfram Language symbol. Default (fetchWeb:false): returns the in-kernel usage message, function signature, options table, and a link to the online documentation — fast, works offline. Set fetchWeb:true to ALSO fetch the full reference page from reference.wolfram.com — includes detailed descriptions, all Method options, notes, and compatibility info. Use fetchWeb:true when the in-kernel result is insufficient (e.g. for complex options like NDSolve Method). Works for user-defined symbols too (in-kernel only for those).

symbol.description: The name of the Wolfram Language symbol to look up (e.g. 'BBrel', 'Solve', 'Signature').

fetchWeb.description: If true, fetch the full reference page from reference.wolfram.com and append it to the in-kernel result. Use for built-in System symbols when you need detailed option descriptions, notes, or compatibility info. Defaults to false.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_insertCells
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Insert one or more cells into the notebook. For a SINGLE cell: pass top-level 'kind' ('code' or 'markdown') and 'content'. For MULTIPLE cells: pass a 'cells' array of {kind, content} objects that will be inserted as a contiguous block. Use 'position' ('before'|'after', default 'after') and 'afterCellId' (preferred) or 'afterCell' (1-based number) to control placement. All inserted code cells are evaluated through the notebook pipeline by default (evaluate defaults to true) — output will appear in the notebook; pass evaluate:false to insert without running. Avoid inserting large duplicate blocks — use wolfbook_editCell to update existing cells.

kind.description: Cell type for single-cell shorthand (use with 'content'). Ignored if 'cells' array is provided.

content.description: Cell source text for single-cell shorthand (use with 'kind'). Ignored if 'cells' array is provided.

cells.description: Ordered list of cells to insert as a contiguous block. Each item: {kind: 'code'|'markdown', content: string}.

kind.description: Cell type: 'code' for Wolfram Language, 'markdown' for text/LaTeX.

position.description: Insert before or after the target cell. Defaults to 'after'.

afterCellId.description: Stable CellId to insert after. Preferred over numeric position after structural edits.

afterCell.description: 1-based cell number to insert after. Use afterCellId when available.

evaluate.description: If true (default), run all inserted code cells through the notebook after insertion — output appears in the notebook and is returned here. Pass false to insert without evaluating.

timeoutSeconds.description: Timeout in seconds for evaluation when evaluate=true. Defaults to 30.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_editCell
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Replaces the source code of one or more cells. SINGLE CELL: provide cellId (preferred, stable) or cellNumber (1-based) plus content. BATCH: provide a 'cells' array of {cellId, content} objects — all cells are edited sequentially and evaluated by default (evaluate defaults to true in batch mode, catching errors immediately). Each item may set evaluate:false to skip its evaluation. Set a top-level timeoutSeconds (default 30) per cell. IMPORTANT: pass real newlines — do not use literal \n; use an actual multi-line string. Content must be syntactically correct Wolfram Language. Accepts 'newContent' as alias for 'content'. Returns diff and eval output per cell.

cellNumber.description: Single-cell mode: 1-based cell number to edit.

cellId.description: Single-cell mode: stable CellId to edit (preferred over cellNumber).

content.description: Single-cell mode: new source text for the cell.

cells.description: Batch mode: array of cells to edit. Each item must have cellId (preferred) or cellNumber, and content. Optionally set evaluate:false on an item to skip evaluation of that cell.

cellId.description: Stable CellId of the cell to edit.

content.description: New source text for this cell.

evaluate.description: Override per-cell evaluation (default: inherits top-level evaluate which defaults to true).
Whether to evaluate after editing. Single-cell default: false. Batch default: true (recommended — catches errors immediately).

timeoutSeconds.description: Max seconds to wait per cell evaluation (default: 30 for batch, 15 for single-cell).

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_runCell
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Execute cells in the notebook. SINGLE CELL MODE: provide 'cellId' (stable identifier, preferred) or 'cellNumber' (1-based) — the cell is re-run with its existing source. There is no 'code' parameter; to run different code use wolfbook_evaluateExpression or first edit the cell with wolfbook_editCell. RANGE MODE: omit cellId/cellNumber and provide 'startCell' and 'endCell' to execute a block of cells. Set 'stopOnError':true (default) to halt on first error. Returns cell output after execution.

cellId.description: Stable CellId of the cell to run (preferred over cellNumber).

cellNumber.description: 1-based cell number to run. Use cellId when available.

startCell.description: Range mode: 1-based number of the first cell to run (inclusive). Omit cellId/cellNumber when using range mode.

endCell.description: Range mode: 1-based number of the last cell to run (inclusive).

stopOnError.description: Range mode: if true (default), stop executing when a cell returns an error message. Set false to run all cells regardless.

timeoutSeconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for evaluation. Defaults to 30.

errorsOnly.description: Range mode: if true, only include cells that produced kernel messages/warnings in the output. Cells with no messages are silently skipped. Default false.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_deleteCell
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Deletes one or more cells from the active Wolfram notebook. Deleted content is saved to ai_deleted_cells.md for recovery (use wolfbook_restoreDeletedCells to undo). Call wolfbook_getNotebookContext first to get CellId values. Prefer cellId/cellIds over cellNumber/cellNumbers because numeric positions shift after structural edits. Cells are removed in descending index order so earlier indices remain accurate. Each deleted cell's content is returned as confirmation.

cellNumber.description: 1-based cell number to delete (single cell). Use cellNumbers for multiple.

cellId.description: Stable CellId to delete (single cell). Preferred over cellNumber after any move/delete operation.

cellNumbers.description: Array of 1-based cell numbers to delete (multiple cells). Cells are deleted in descending index order.

cellIds.description: Array of stable CellId values to delete (multiple cells). Preferred over cellNumbers after structural edits.

saveToRecovery.description: If true (default), save deleted cell content to ai_deleted_cells.md before removing.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_searchCells
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Searches notebook cells for a given query string or regex pattern. Returns matching cell numbers, CellId values, source previews, and whether the match was in the source code, output, or both. Use this to quickly locate cells containing a specific variable, function, or error message without reading the entire notebook. Useful in long notebooks before calling wolfbook_getNotebookContext with a targeted startCell/endCell range.

query.description: The text or regex pattern to search for (case-insensitive).

regex.description: If true, treat query as a regular expression. Default: false (plain text search).

kind.description: Optional: restrict search to only code or only markdown cells.

includeOutput.description: If true (default), also search cell outputs, not just source code.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_getKernelState
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns a summary of the current Wolfram kernel state: all user-defined symbols matching a context pattern, showing their values (for direct assignments) or rule counts (for functions with DownValues). Default pattern 'Global`*' shows everything defined interactively. Use a narrower pattern like 'QSC`*' to inspect a specific package context. Call this before inserting or editing code to understand what is already defined and avoid naming conflicts.

pattern.description: Wolfram context pattern to match symbols against (default: 'Global`*'). Examples: 'Global`*', 'QSC`*', 'Global`Q*'.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_moveCell
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Move or copy a cell within a notebook or between two open notebooks. Within one notebook: reorders atomically. Cross-notebook: reads source cell, inserts into target, then removes from source (or keeps it if copy:true). Use sourceNotebook/targetNotebook to specify notebooks by filename; omit both to use the active notebook as both source and destination. Prefer cellId/afterCellId for stable targeting (numbers shift after edits).

cellId.description: Stable CellId of the source cell. Preferred over cellNumber after structural edits.

cellNumber.description: 1-based number of the cell to move/copy in the source notebook.

toPosition.description: Insert after this 1-based cell number in the target notebook. Use 0 to insert at the very beginning.

afterCellId.description: Stable CellId in the target notebook to insert after. Preferred over toPosition.

sourceNotebook.description: Filename of the source notebook (e.g. 'solver.wb'). Omit to use the active notebook.

targetNotebook.description: Filename of the destination notebook (e.g. 'main.wb'). Omit to move/copy within the same notebook.

copy.description: If true, copy the cell (leave source intact). If false or omitted, move it (delete from source).

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_restoreDeletedCells
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists or restores recently deleted cells from the ai_deleted_cells.md recovery log maintained by wolfbook_deleteCell. Use action="list" to browse the last N deleted cells (default 10) — useful to review what was just removed or to confirm what to restore. Use action="restore" to re-insert the last N deleted cells at a specified position (default: end of notebook). Prefer afterCellId for stable insertion after a specific target cell. The recovery log is never cleared.

action.description: "list" to show recent deleted cells; "restore" to re-insert them into the notebook.

count.description: How many recent deletions to list or restore (default: 10 for list, 1 for restore).

insertPosition.description: Where to insert restored cells: "end" (default) or a 1-based cell number N (inserts after Cell N). Use 0 to insert before Cell 1.

afterCellId.description: Optional stable CellId to restore after. Preferred over insertPosition after structural edits.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_kernelControl
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Kernel lifecycle control. action='restart': restart the Wolfram Language kernel (clears all definitions and memory — use only when stuck or crashed). action='abort': abort the currently running evaluation without restarting (safe when a cell is hung). action='checkpoint': save a snapshot of all Global` definitions to a temp .mx file (fast, safe, non-destructive). action='restore': reload a previous checkpoint — ClearAll Global` then Get the .mx file. Use checkpoint/restore to create safe rollback points before risky refactors. Check wolfbook_getKernelState first to confirm kernel state before acting.

action.description: 'restart' to restart the kernel (destructive — clears all state). 'abort' to stop the current evaluation. 'checkpoint' to save all Global` definitions to a .mx file. 'restore' to reload Global` state from a previous checkpoint.

tag.description: Optional label for the checkpoint file (e.g. 'before-refactor'). Only used with action='checkpoint'.

path.description: Path to a specific .mx checkpoint file to restore. Only used with action='restore'. If omitted, restores the most recent checkpoint from this session.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_kernelCrashLog
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Reads the Wolfram kernel debug log (img/<notebookName>/wolfram-kernel-debug.log) and/or macOS crash reports (~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/) to help diagnose kernel crashes and unexpected disconnections. The debug log lives next to btl.log in the notebook's img/ subfolder and is recreated fresh each kernel start. Crash reports contain stack traces from kernel aborts. Use source="debug" for the live debug log, source="crash" for crash reports, source="all" for both.

source.description: "debug" (default) reads the kernel debug log from img/<notebookName>/; "crash" reads macOS DiagnosticReports; "all" reads both.

lines.description: How many tail lines of the debug log to return (default: 150, max: 1000).

filter.description: Optional keyword or regex to filter log lines (case-insensitive). E.g. "ERROR", "ABORT", "crash".

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_findPackage
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Searches for Wolfram Language packages on the Wolfram Paclet Server (via PacletFindRemote) and on GitHub. Returns names, descriptions, and ready-to-run install commands for each result. For Paclet Server hits the result includes the exact PacletInstall["Name"] command; for GitHub hits it includes the releases URL and explains both the .paclet-URL install path and the URLDownload+ExtractArchive+AppendTo[$Path]+Get workflow for plain source repos. After finding a package, use wolfbook_evaluateExpression with timeoutSeconds>=120 to run the install command — do NOT guess install syntax, always use the commands returned by this tool.

query.description: Search term, e.g. "numerical ODE", "quantum field theory", "cluster algebra". Alphanumeric words and hyphens only.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_debugCell
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Controls the Wolfbook step-through debugger. Use action="analyze" to inspect a cell's step structure before debugging. Use action="start" to begin a debug session on a cell (kernel pauses at first step). Use action="status" to check if a session is active and see the last known step info. Use action="stepOver" to execute the current statement and pause at the next one at the same or outer loop level. Use action="stepInto" to enter an inner loop body (pauses at first statement inside). Use action="stepOut" to finish the current loop level and return to the parent. Use action="continue" to run until the next breakpoint. Use action="runToEnd" to run the cell to completion ignoring breakpoints. Use action="stop" to abort the debug session. All step/continue/stop commands require an active session (check with action="status"). Timings are recorded automatically and shown as inline annotations after each session. Use action="addBreakpoint" with a "line" number (1-based) and optional "cellId" or "cellNumber" to set a breakpoint; use action="removeBreakpoint" similarly to remove one; action="clearBreakpoints" removes all (or all for a specific cell if cellId/cellNumber is given); action="listBreakpoints" shows all current breakpoints. Use action="addWatch" with "variableName" to add a variable to the Watch Panel; action="removeWatch" to remove one; action="listWatch" to see the current watch list.

action.description: The operation to perform. Use analyze or start before session; use step/continue/stop while paused; use addBreakpoint/removeBreakpoint/clearBreakpoints/listBreakpoints for breakpoint management; use addWatch/removeWatch/listWatch for the Watch Panel variable list.

cellNumber.description: 1-based cell number for action=analyze, action=start, action=addBreakpoint, action=removeBreakpoint, or action=clearBreakpoints. Omit to use the currently selected cell.

cellId.description: Stable CellId for action=analyze, action=start, action=addBreakpoint, action=removeBreakpoint, or action=clearBreakpoints. Preferred over cellNumber after reordering.

line.description: 1-based line number within the cell. Required for action=addBreakpoint and action=removeBreakpoint.

variableName.description: Wolfram Language variable name for action=addWatch or action=removeWatch.

showInstrumentedCode.description: For action=analyze: if true (default), include the full instrumented code in the result.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_fileOps
languageModelTools.modelDescription: File system operations on the local machine. action='read': read the text contents of the file at 'path' (required). action='write': write 'content' string to 'path' (required, creates or overwrites). action='list': list files and subdirectories under directory 'path' (optional, defaults to workspace root); use 'ext' to filter by extension (e.g. '.wl'), 'depth' to control recursion depth (default 4, max 8). All paths should be absolute.

action.description: 'read' to read file contents, 'write' to write file, 'list' to list directory.

path.description: Absolute path to the file or directory. Required for action='read' and action='write'. For action='list', defaults to the first workspace root folder if omitted.

content.description: Text content to write. Required for action='write'.

ext.description: File extension filter for action='list' (e.g. '.wl', '.m'). If omitted, all files are returned.

depth.description: Recursion depth for action='list'. 1 = immediate children only, no subdirectory traversal. Defaults to 4, max 8.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_runTerminal
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Runs a shell command and returns stdout/stderr. Use for project-level tasks like builds, tests, scripts, and LaTeX compilation. Keep commands scoped to the workspace.

cwd.description: Optional absolute working directory. Defaults to workspace root.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_paperSearch
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Search academic papers (HEP/math/physics) via INSPIRE-HEP with arXiv fallback. Five actions: (1) 'search' — find papers by title, author, abstract, arXiv ID, INSPIRE texkey, or freeform query; results include title, authors, year, INSPIRE citation count, abstract, ar5iv HTML link, and INSPIRE URL. (2) 'bibtex' — fetch a full BibTeX @article record from INSPIRE. (3) 'bibitem' — fetch a LaTeX \bibitem record (INSPIRE latex-us format). (4) 'references' — list all papers cited BY a paper from INSPIRE (34+ entries typical); add includeContexts:true to also fetch from Semantic Scholar the exact sentences in which each reference is cited. (5) 'citations' — list papers that CITE a given paper, with citation context sentences from Semantic Scholar. Identifier formats accepted: new arXiv IDs ('2103.15840'), old arXiv IDs ('hep-th/0212208'), INSPIRE texkeys ('Gromov:2013pga'), or numeric INSPIRE record IDs. arXiv IDs are resolved via the INSPIRE /api/arxiv/<id> endpoint for reliable lookup. Falls back to arXiv API search for non-HEP papers. Use this tool any time you need to find, cite, or survey academic papers.

author.description: Search by author name (for 'search' action). Use 'Lastname' or 'Lastname, Firstname'.

identifier.description: arXiv ID (e.g. '2103.15840'), INSPIRE texkey (e.g. 'Gromov:2014caa'), or INSPIRE record ID. Used for search (by ID), bibtex, bibitem, references, citations.

query.description: Freeform INSPIRE search query (advanced). Combined with title/author/abstract if both provided.

includeAbstract.description: Include abstracts in search results. Default: true.

includeContexts.description: For 'references' action: also fetch citation contexts from Semantic Scholar showing HOW each reference is used in the text. Default: false.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results (default: 5 for search, 10 for citations, max 20/50).

languageModelTools.name: wolfteam_proposePlan
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Call this tool when you have formulated a multi-step calculation plan and need the user to approve it before you begin executing. Pass the plan summary and list of steps. The user will see the plan in a confirmation dialog and click Allow to approve, or Deny to reject. Do NOT execute any steps until this tool returns successfully.

planSummary.description: One-paragraph summary of what the plan will accomplish

steps.description: Ordered list of steps to execute

languageModelTools.name: wolfteam_askDecision
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Call this tool when you reach a conceptual decision point — a choice of gauge, coordinate system, ansatz, expansion strategy, or any fork where the user's physics expertise should guide the direction. Present the question, the available options, and a default. The user can edit the selectedOption parameter before approving. Do NOT guess — always call this tool at genuine decision points.

selectedOption.description: The user's selected option — user can edit this before clicking Allow

context.description: Brief context for why this decision matters

languageModelTools.name: wolfteam_checkpoint
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Call this tool after completing a significant calculation step to show the user the intermediate result and what comes next. The user clicks Allow to continue or Deny to pause and inspect. Use between major steps, not after every trivial evaluation.

result.description: The key result or output (keep concise)

nextStep.description: What will be done next if user approves

languageModelTools.name: wolfteam_askSpecialist
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Call this tool when you need the user's expert input to make a strategic decision — e.g., which paper's conventions to follow, which ansatz to use, which branch of a solution to explore, or which notation to adopt. The question is rendered in Markdown+LaTeX inside the Wolfbook 'Ask Specialist' panel with a blinking background and audio alert so the user notices it. The tool blocks until the user types a reply and submits it. Use this instead of guessing on questions that only the domain expert can answer correctly.

question.description: The question to ask the specialist. May contain Markdown formatting and LaTeX math ($ inline, $$ display). Be specific and concrete.

context.description: Optional background context for the question — e.g., the current approach, relevant equations, or why this decision matters. Rendered above the question.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_getContext
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns full deck context: open files, current theme, available theme presets, renderer capabilities (KaTeX math, fragmentOrder animation, eval blocks, CSS color classes), and best-practice tips. ALWAYS call this first before creating or editing slides — it tells you everything the renderer supports. Use the 'file' parameter to target a specific open .wslide file.

file.description: Optional: filename or path of the .wslide file to target. Defaults to the active slide editor.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_listSlides
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns a rich multi-line text summary of all slides in the deck. Each slide entry includes: index, id, label, hidden status, step count (animation fragments), character count, and an indented ASCII block tree showing block types, content excerpts, and image ALT/src info. Pass verbose:true to include the full ASCII block diagram for every slide — useful for inspecting multiple slides at once without calling wolfslide_getSlide in a loop. Use the 'file' parameter to target a specific open .wslide file.

file.description: Optional: filename or path of the .wslide file to target. Defaults to the active slide editor.

verbose.description: If true, include the full ASCII block tree for every slide in the listing. Useful to inspect multiple slides at once without looping wolfslide_getSlide calls.

docUri.description: Optional: target a specific open .wslide file.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_getSlide
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the full block tree, ASCII diagram, image summary, and raw JSON for a single slide. Defaults to the currently visible slide when no index is given. Accepts slideIndex (1-based), slideNumber (alias), or slideId. Use this after wolfslide_listSlides to inspect an individual slide.

slideIndex.description: 1-based slide index. Defaults to currently visible slide if omitted.

docUri.description: Optional: target a specific open .wslide file.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_getSlideHtml
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Renders a single slide to standalone Reveal.js HTML and returns it inline (or writes to outputPath). Much faster than wolfslide_exportHtml for checking one slide's layout. Use this to verify layout, typography, and image sizing without exporting the full deck. Accepts slideIndex (1-based), slideNumber (alias), or slideId. Defaults to the currently visible slide.

slideIndex.description: 1-based slide index. Defaults to currently visible slide if omitted.

outputPath.description: Optional absolute path to write the HTML file. If omitted, HTML is returned inline.

docUri.description: Optional: target a specific open .wslide file.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_getImageDimensions
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns {width, height, format} for a PNG, JPEG, or WebP image given a local file path or http/https URL. Only reads the first 512 bytes (Range header for URLs). Use this before inserting an image block to get correct w/h values — required because image style.maxHeight/maxWidth only constrain the wrapper div, not the image itself, without explicit w/h on the block.

src.description: Local absolute file path or http/https URL of the image.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_duplicateSlide
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Clones a slide (with all its blocks) and inserts the copy immediately after the original. All block IDs are regenerated. Useful for reveal-step variants and before/after comparisons.

slideIndex.description: 1-based index of the slide to duplicate. Defaults to currently visible slide.

docUri.description: Optional: target a specific open .wslide file.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_insertSlide
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Inserts a single slide. For inserting many slides at once, prefer wolfslide_bulkInsert. Content nodes support: KaTeX math via $...$ (inline) and $$...$$ (display); fragmentOrder:N for step-by-step animation; CSS classes .gl .te .ro .mu .bl .re .cy for colored text (via text). Set slide.background to match your theme. If afterIndex is omitted, appends at the end.

slide.description: Slide object. Required fields: label. Optional: background, layout, children, gap, padding.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_editSlide
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Replaces top-level properties of a slide (label, background, layout, gap, padding, hidden, children). Only keys present in the patch are updated. To rewrite a slide's block tree, pass the complete children array. Merge semantics: in the children array, a block specified as {"id":"..."}  with no other fields is a no-op stub — the existing block is kept unchanged. Valid block types: container, heading, text, image, list, math, box, raw, code, arrow, eval. Unknown types are silently stored but will not render — a warning is returned. Content supports KaTeX math ($...$, $$...$$) and fragmentOrder:N animation. CSS color classes: .gl .te .ro .mu .bl .re .cy.

patch.description: Object with fields to update on the slide.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_deleteSlide
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Removes a slide by 1-based index or id.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_moveSlide
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Moves a slide to a new position. toIndex is 1-based (the desired final position).

toIndex.description: Target 1-based index. Use 1 to move to the first position. Using 0 is treated the same as 1.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_undo
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Triggers undo in the active .wslide editor, reverting the last change. Useful after making a mistake. Optionally specify docUri to target a specific file.

docUri.description: Optional URI of the .wslide file to undo in. Defaults to the active editor.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_saveFile
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Persists the current deck to disk. Call after editing slides to ensure changes are saved.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_exportHtml
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Exports the deck as a standalone Reveal.js HTML file (images inlined as data URIs). Returns the path of the exported file.

outputPath.description: Optional output file path. Defaults to <deckName>.html next to the .wslide file.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_insertEvalBlock
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Inserts a Mathematica evaluable block on a slide. Graphics (Plot, Graphics, etc.) render as crisp SVG; symbolic expressions (Integrate, Series, etc.) render as beautifully typeset LaTeX via KaTeX; fallback is PNG. Auto-evaluates immediately by default. Use this for computed plots, formulas, diagrams, or any dynamic Wolfram Language output in presentations.

parentBlockId.description: Optional parent container block id to insert into.

w.description: Image width in pixels for rasterization. Default: 800.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_runEvalBlock
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Evaluates (or re-evaluates) an existing eval block on a slide. Optionally updates the input expression before running. Graphics produce SVG, symbolic math produces LaTeX (KaTeX), with PNG fallback. Returns the evaluation result type (svg/latex/image/text/error).

input.description: Optional new Mathematica expression. If omitted, re-runs the existing input.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_setTheme
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Sets the deck's color theme from a preset or custom values. Presets: 'academic-light' (white/navy, formal), 'dark-modern' (dark/gold/teal, tech), 'dark-navy' (deep navy/blue), 'solarized-dark' (warm dark), 'high-contrast' (black/neon), 'warm-cream' (light warm). Also updates slide backgrounds to match. Call wolfslide_getContext to see all presets with descriptions. For custom themes, pass a theme object with keys: navy, blue, cyan, accent, editorCSS.

theme.description: Custom theme object with color keys: navy, blue, cyan, accent, editorCSS. Used when preset is not specified.

defaultBackground.description: Background color to apply to all slides that currently have default backgrounds.

applyBackground.description: Whether to update slide backgrounds to match the preset. Default: true.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_bulkInsert
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Inserts multiple slides in one call — use this when building a presentation from scratch instead of calling insertSlide repeatedly. Accepts an array of slide objects, an optional theme (preset name or object), and optional meta. Content nodes support: KaTeX math via $...$ / $$...$$; fragmentOrder:N for animation; CSS color classes .gl .te .ro .mu .bl .re .cy; eval blocks for Mathematica-generated graphics. Tip: call wolfslide_getContext first to see theme presets and renderer capabilities.

slides.description: Array of slide objects. Each slide: {label, background, layout, gap, padding, children:[...blocks]}. Block types: text, heading, image, list, container, code, eval, arrow, raw, box.

afterIndex.description: Insert after this 1-based index. 0 = prepend. Default: append at end.

theme.description: Theme preset name (string) or custom theme object to apply to the deck.

meta.description: Deck metadata to set, e.g. {title: 'My Talk', author: 'Name'}.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_getCellOutput
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Read the current text/plain output of a single notebook cell without re-running it. Returns the result and any kernel messages shown below the cell.

cellId.description: Stable CellId of the cell (preferred over cellNumber).

cellNumber.description: 1-based cell number. Use cellId when available.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_validateSyntax
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Check Wolfram Language syntax in one or more cells using the kernel's SyntaxQ. Returns a list of cells with syntax errors. Falls back to offline bracket-matching when the kernel is not running.

cellId.description: Stable CellId to validate (single cell, preferred over cellNumber after reordering).

cellNumber.description: Check a single cell by 1-based number. Use cellId when available.

endCell.description: Range: last cell to check (inclusive, 1-based). Defaults to last cell.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_latex
languageModelTools.modelDescription: LaTeX workflow tool: save .tex files, compile to PDF via latexmk, and parse compilation errors. Actions: 'save' writes .tex to disk, 'compile' runs latexmk, 'errors' parses the .log for errors/warnings, 'build' does save→compile→errors in one call. Requires latexmk (TeX Live / MacTeX).

action.description: save: write .tex to disk. compile: run latexmk. errors: parse .log for errors. build: save + compile + return errors.

path.description: Path to .tex file (absolute or relative to notebook dir).

content.description: LaTeX source content (required for 'save' and 'build' actions).

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_searchSlides
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Search across all slides for blocks matching a query. Supports three filter dimensions that can be combined: "query" (case-insensitive text match against block content, alt, src, label), "blockType" (filter by exact block type: "text", "heading", "image", "container", "list", "code", "eval", "arrow", "raw"), "styleKey"+"styleValue" (find blocks with a specific CSS style property, e.g. styleKey="color" styleValue="navy"). Returns matching slide indices, ids, block ids, types, and content previews. Use this to locate specific blocks for editing without reading the full deck.

query.description: Text to search for (case-insensitive). Optional when blockType or styleKey is provided.

docUri.description: Optional: target a specific open .wslide file.

styleKey.description: Style property name to filter on (e.g. "color", "fontSize", "background"). Combined with styleValue for exact matching.

styleValue.description: Style property value to match (partial, case-insensitive). Requires styleKey.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_block
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Block-level operations on slide blocks. action="insert": add a new block to a slide. action="edit": patch a block's properties by blockId (pass updates or patch object). action="delete": remove a block by blockId. action="move": relocate a block within or between containers. action="bulkEdit": apply many block edits in one atomic save — pass edits:[{blockId, updates, slideId?}] for batch layout fixes (e.g. adjusting padding across 10 slides). Only one applyDeck call is made for the whole batch.

action.description: insert: add a new block. edit: patch block properties. delete: remove a block. move: relocate a block. bulkEdit: apply multiple block edits in one save.

block.description: Block object to insert (required for 'insert'). Include type, content, etc.

updates.description: Properties to patch on the block (for "edit"). Also accepted as "patch" for consistency with wolfslide_editSlide.

docUri.description: Optional: target a specific open .wslide file.

edits.description: Array of block edits for action="bulkEdit". Each item: {blockId, updates (or patch), slideId? or slideIndex?}. blockId is required; slideId/slideIndex are optional (auto-searched across all slides if omitted).

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_advanced
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Advanced slide operations. Actions: 'duplicate' deep-copies a slide (new ids assigned), 'check' audits the entire deck for issues (empty slides, missing alt-text, fragment gaps, duplicate labels), 'reorderFragments' sets animation step order on a slide, 'measure' returns rendered block sizes and detects overflow.

action.description: duplicate: copy a slide. check: audit deck for issues. reorderFragments: set animation order. measure: get rendered block sizes.

order.description: Fragment order array for 'reorderFragments'. Each entry: blockId string or {blockId, step} object.

docUri.description: Optional: target a specific open .wslide file.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_imageAsset
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Manage image assets for the active .wslide deck. Image files live in img/<deckName>.wslide/ next to the .wslide file. Each image can have a sidecar annotation file (.ann.json) with description, source, and tags. Actions: 'list' — show all images with sizes, dimensions, which slides use them, and any annotation; 'info' — full details + ready-to-paste block JSON for one image; 'copy' — import an external image file into the deck folder (returns the relative src path and a ready-to-use block snippet); 'delete' — remove an image (warns if still referenced by a block, use force:true to override); 'rename' — rename a file AND automatically update all block src references in the deck; 'annotate' — write/update description, source, tags for an image (stored in .ann.json sidecar beside the image); 'insert' — copy an image AND immediately insert an image block into a slide in one combined call. Block src format: "img/<deckName>.wslide/<filename>". Always use this tool to add images — never construct src paths manually.

action.description: list: all images. info: details for one file. copy: import external file. delete: remove file. rename: rename + update refs. annotate: set description/source/tags. insert: copy + add block to slide.

filename.description: Target filename within the deck's img/ folder (e.g. 'spectrum_plot.png'). Used by: info, delete, rename, annotate, insert.

srcPath.description: Absolute path to the source file on disk. Used by: copy, insert.

annotation.description: String (description) or object {description, source, tags[]} to save as .ann.json sidecar. Used by: copy, insert, annotate.

slideIndex.description: 1-based slide index to insert the image block into. Used by: insert.

slideId.description: Slide id (alternative to slideIndex). Used by: insert.

targetBlockId.description: If provided, the image block is appended as a child of this container block (for insertion into nested layouts). Used by: insert.

w.description: Display width in pixels for the inserted image block. Defaults to image's native width (capped at 1600).

h.description: Display height in pixels for the inserted image block. Defaults to image's native height (capped at 900).

fit.description: Object-fit mode for the inserted image block. Default: 'contain'.

style.description: Optional CSS style object for the inserted image block.

fragmentOrder.description: Animation step for the inserted image block.

force.description: For action:'delete' — delete even if the image is still referenced by slide blocks.

docUri.description: Optional: target a specific open .wslide file.

[wolfram].editor.fontFamily: Menlo, Monaco, 'Courier New', 'STIX Two Math', 'Noto Sans Math', 'Cambria Math', monospace
